## Today's Agenda

- A report that rebuilds itself from the code
- IMRaD, and the three transparency markers the Methods must carry
- Two studio blocks: the paper, then the poster
- Publishing the site, and the checks that run before it goes live

## The Last Meeting

[Studio session]{.eyebrow}

- **Two working blocks: the White Paper, then the poster**
    - Short input between them; the rest of the evening is your working time
    - Help is in the room all evening
- **What you build tonight is what you submit**
- **Leave with a rendered site, a poster layout, and a draft reflection**

## Done, and Not Finished

- **The study has every hard part behind it**
    - A question, a theory, and a reliability-tested codebook
    - A defensible sample, a clean dataset, three figures, and a finding
- **And it still lives in pieces**
    - A codebook here, a script there, output that scrolled past

A study scattered across a dozen files is raw material. Tonight gives it a form.

## A Report That Rebuilds Itself

- **The ordinary way to write up a study is quietly fragile**
    - Run the analysis, copy the numbers, screenshot the figures, write around them
    - Change one coding rule and every pasted number is stale
    - Nothing in the document tells you so
- **The alternative: put the analysis inside the document**
    - A **Quarto document** interleaves prose with live code chunks

## Numbers You Never Type

```markdown
The analysis dataset held `r nrow(analysis)` coded messages,
of which `r sum(!is.na(analysis$is_gaming))` carried a
gaming-status label.
```

In the rendered report those backtick expressions become the actual counts, so nothing in
the sentence can fall out of date.

## Figures You Never Paste

```r
#| label: fig-msglen
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Message length by channel type."

ggplot(msglen, aes(message_length, fill = is_gaming)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5) +
  v2v::theme_v2v()
```

Those lines sit inside an `{r}` chunk in the report, so the figure is produced at render
time rather than pasted in.

## Two Payoffs That Matter

- **The report cannot drift from the analysis, because the report is the analysis**
- **The report can be checked**
    - Anyone with the source files and the data renders the same results (Peng, 2011)

The idea predates Quarto and R. Runnable code and its prose in one document is what Knuth
named literate programming in 1984, and the "one click" is the render button.

## IMRaD, and What Each Section Owes the Reader

- **Introduction:** the question and why it matters, built from your Research Proposal
- **Methods:** what was done, in enough detail for someone else to repeat it
    - The codebook, the sampling, the reliability check, and the wrangling
- **Results:** what was found, without interpretation
    - The figures, the means, and the test statistic with its df, p-value, and effect size
- **Discussion:** what the result means, plus the honest limits

An abstract goes in front, and the references at the back.

## The White Paper, Specifically

- **IMRaD structure, in APA 7 throughout**
- **Effect sizes, confidence intervals, and power statistics, not only p-values**
- **A pre-registration disclosure in the Methods**
- **A Discussion that situates the finding in your theoretical literature**

Converting your results into IMRaD costs something. Ask what is lost in the conversion, and what must be added.

## Methods, Three Transparency Markers

1. A **data provenance** statement: where the data came from, the date range, and what was excluded and why
2. A **reliability** report: the statistic, its value, the procedure, the threshold, and the single-coder limitation named as such
3. The **pre-registration disclosure**: the dated file in your project repository, cited by path and commit, and every departure from it

Each marker signals that the study meets the standard it claims. Any analysis beyond the
plan is labeled **exploratory**.

## What Preregistration Is For

> "Preregistration distinguishes analyses and outcomes that result from predictions from
> those that result from postdictions."
>
> Nosek et al. (2018, p. 2600)

- **Preregistration is not a promise of virtue. It makes one distinction legible: what was planned and what was found afterwards**
- **Draft your disclosure sentence tonight**
    - List every departure from your plan, and say how you report each one

## Where the 200 Points Sit

- **Introduction and framing:** 25
- **Methods:** 55
- **Results:** 40
- **Discussion:** 40
- **Abstract and references:** 15
- **Reproducibility and publication:** 15
- **Reflection:** 10

Methods carries the most weight because it carries the three transparency markers.

## Exercise: Not Only a Threshold {.discuss}

[Wasserstein and Lazar (2016)]{.eyebrow}

> "Scientific conclusions and business or policy decisions should not be based only on
> whether a p-value passes a specific threshold."
>
> Wasserstein and Lazar (2016, p. 131)

The word doing the work in that sentence is *only*. Answer each in writing:

- Name two things your White Paper reports beside the p-value, such as the effect size or the confidence interval
- Describe what would convince a reader who ignores your p-value entirely

## One Book, Many Chapters

```yaml
project:
  type: book
book:
  title: "White Paper"
  chapters:
    - index.qmd
    - 01-introduction.qmd
    - 02-methods.qmd
    - 03-results.qmd
    - 04-discussion.qmd
    - 05-reflection.qmd
    - references.qmd
```

`_quarto.yml` lists the chapters in order. `new_portfolio()` wrote it for you, with the
codebook and the journal as appendices. Set the title to your own.

## Studio Block One

[White Paper]{.eyebrow}

- **Get `index.qmd` rendering, even if it is mostly headings**
- **Move your Results section into `03-results.qmd` first, since you already have it**
- **Replace every pasted number with an inline `r` expression**
- **Replace every pasted figure with a chunk that produces it**
- **Then write the Discussion paragraph that reports both the size and the significance of your result**

## Going Live

```r
v2v::deploy_portfolio()
```

```
── Pre-flight checks ──
✔ renv library in sync
✔ no uncommitted changes
✔ _quarto.yml valid
ℹ Rendering 9 pages ... done
ℹ Publishing to GitHub Pages ... done
✔ Portfolio live on GitHub Pages.
```

## The Three Pre-Flight Checks

- **renv in sync:** the site is built with the package versions the source declares
- **No uncommitted changes:** the live site matches what is saved
- **`_quarto.yml` valid:** the render will not fail partway through

Each check heads off one demoralizing failure, the worst being a collapse the night the
portfolio is due. The checks exist so the last step of a long study is the calm one.

## The Poster

- **36 by 24 inches, in landscape orientation**
- **Title, authors, and institution, plus a 100-word abstract**
- **Background and hypotheses, then the methods in condensed form**
- **Key results, with one or two `theme_v2v()` figures**
- **Discussion and implications, plus a QR code to your pre-registration or portfolio**

## What Earns Space on a Poster

- **A poster is a ninety-second pitch, not a paper at a larger font**
- **Pick the one figure that lands the finding in thirty seconds**
    - Give that figure the most space on the board
- **Cut every sentence that shows effort rather than result**
- **Numbers survive the cut. Hedges do not**

Your reader is standing up, holding a drink, four feet away.

## Studio Block Two

[Poster]{.eyebrow}

- **Sketch the layout on paper first, in blocks, before opening any software**
- **Place your chosen figure, then build the text around it**
- **Write the 100-word abstract last, once the blocks exist**
- **Generate the QR code from the URL the deploy gave you**
- **Read your title aloud, and cut it if it takes two breaths**

## Common Failures in the Last Week

- **The site renders on your machine and nowhere else, because renv drifted**
- **A figure vanishes from the site**
    - Its chunk depends on an object that exists only in your console
- **The poster is exported at screen resolution and printed at 36 inches, so it is blurry**
- **The QR code points at a private repository**

Test the whole chain tonight, on a machine you did not build it on.

## The Reflection

- **One paragraph, and the portfolio is incomplete without it**
    - What turned out harder than expected
    - What the dataset could not answer, and why
    - What a second attempt would change
- **Avoid both the bland version ("it went well") and the anxious version ("it all went wrong")**

A reflection is evidence of judgment, not an apology.

## Checkpoint Before You Leave

You should have:

- A portfolio site that renders locally with no errors
- A Results section with zero hand-typed numbers
- A published URL, and a QR code pointing at it
- A poster layout with its main figure chosen and placed
- The reflection paragraph drafted, even roughly

## From Vibes to Variables

- **A question became a design, and the design became data**
- **The data became figures and a test**
- **All of it became a site another person can check and extend**
- **The shared example happened to be Twitch chat. Nothing in the method depended on that, and your own study proves it**

The distance from vibes to variables is the whole of research methods, and you have now
walked it once.
